uncited: This family covers algorithmic variants of the Marching Cubes isosurface extraction method that modify input data, lookup logic, vertex placement, or post-processing to address topological ambiguity, mesh quality, computational efficiency, or data uncertainty.

It sets itself apart from standard MC by introducing preprocessing, dynamic state propagation, geometric snapping, or error-aware interpolation to resolve artifacts, speed up processing, or attach metadata to the surface.
All variants operate on a structured 3D grid and produce a triangle mesh, building on [Marching Cubes Lookup and Configuration](2518-marching-cubes-lookup-and-configuration.md).

The core mechanism of determining edge intersections via a case index (derived from vertex signs relative to an isovalue) remains foundational, though how this index is computed and how resulting triangles are formed varies.
**Definition**: A disambiguation technique for Marching Cubes used to ensure topological consistency across multiresolution boundaries.
**Steps**: For each cell, determine which corners are above or below the isovalue to identify intersecting edges.
Use the modified triangulation table to decide how to triangulate the isosurface within the cell.
Calculate vertex positions by linearly interpolating along the intersecting cell edges.
Store calculated vertices in a hash table keyed by the edge they lie on to avoid redundant calculations.
Compute normals for each triangle using a cross-product and store them in the same hash table.
